name: Evernote
description: Evernote is a note-taking and organization app for capturing, structuring, and retrieving notes, documents, and web content, with tools for tasks, calendar linking, and team collaboration.
best_for: Vendor copy targets general users organizing personal information, teams doing real-time collaborative work, students, and enterprise customers.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.notes: Capped at 50 notes total, 1 notebook, 200MB of attachments, and sync limited to 1 device.

tiers.name: Starter
tiers.notes: $99/year billed annually, or $14.99/month billed month-to-month. Up to 1,000 notes, 20 notebooks, 1,000 attachments, sync on 3 devices, 5GB storage. Replaced the older Personal plan in late 2025.

tiers.name: Advanced
tiers.notes: $249.99/year billed annually, or about $24.99/month month-to-month. Unlimited notes, notebooks, and attachments, unlimited device sync, and AI search/edit features. Replaced the older Professional plan.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.notes: Contact sales; offers a separate 14-day free trial versus 7 days for Starter/Advanced.

cons: The Free plan is capped at just 50 notes total and syncs to only 1 device, so a free user cannot use Evernote across a phone and a laptop simultaneously.
Even the cheapest paid tier (Starter) is not unlimited — it still caps notes at 1,000, notebooks at 20, and device sync at 3 devices; only the top Advanced tier removes these caps.

In late 2025 Evernote discontinued its long-standing Personal and Professional plan names and pricing and replaced them with the pricier Starter and Advanced tiers, migrating existing users onto the new pricing.
features: Notebooks and Spaces for organizing notes
Full-text and fast search across notes
Calendar integration linking events to notes
Web Clipper for saving web content

alternatives.name: Notion
alternatives.description: An all-in-one workspace combining documents, databases, project tracking, and team knowledge.
alternatives.best_for: People who want databases and project tracking alongside notes

alternatives.name: Obsidian
alternatives.description: A note-taking app that stores notes as local Markdown files and links them into a personal knowledge base.
alternatives.best_for: People who want local-first, privately owned notes

alternatives.name: Coda
alternatives.description: A collaborative document platform that combines text, tables, formulas, and app-like workflows.
alternatives.best_for: Teams wanting notes that grow into structured team tools
